_about: ShadowVeil's built world (Alpha 0.4.2): the exteriors of the seven kingdoms, their streets' houses, walls, gates, bridges, aqueducts, ruins, landmarks and the mouths of every documented underground place. Transcribed from projectrpg.txt (WORLD BUILDING and each kingdom's Major Locations), which has the final say. 'at' is a chunk [x, z] as the document gives it (x west to east, z south to north, fractions allowed); 'size' is [front width, depth] in cells; 'facing' is the way the front looks (n, s, e, w, or 'road': toward the nearest road). (0.4.2) Every building keeps its rooms' volumes empty for its interior (0.4.3), every dungeon its volume beyond the sealed door; the building registry (registry.json, registry.md) records and checks them all.

architecture._palettes: (0.4.2, gamefixes: building textures unique per building in each territory) a material given as a list is the territory's palette for it - each building draws its own from it by its seed, so no two neighbours are alike while the street keeps its culture; each kingdom's own walling leads its walls.
architecture._standards: (0.4.2, gamefixes: consistent architectural standards for every structure, ready for its interior in 0.4.3) the measures every enterable building is held to (cells: one metre). wallThickness: an outer wall's depth; storeyMin: floor-to-floor height (a floor's cell, then its clear room); clearMin: the clear height of a room under its ceiling (3 = a tall man under a beam); doorClear: a doorway's clear width and height; sillHeight: a window's sill over its floor; stairShaft: the open well a storey's stair climbs through (width, length); areaPerBed: floor area a sleeper needs with room to move; headroomUnderRoof: the clear height an attic needs to be a room; foundationDepth: how far a footing runs below a slope's low edge; undergroundCover: rock left between a reserved underground volume and the ground over it; obstructionPercent: how much of an interior volume may be taken by what stands in it besides its floors (a pillar, a stair's hood, a corner turret's footing).
architecture._purposes: (0.4.2) what each kind of building is for, read by the building registry: whether it is entered, its floors when its height is one lofty room (floors) or its storeys' height when not the standard's (storeyHeight), the rooms its interior will be built into in 0.4.3 (rooms), the least floor area (m2) its work needs (minArea), the beds it must hold (beds: a count; perResident: one for each person whose home it is), and whether it must have a floor above (minFloors). purposeRules give a structure its purpose by its template or its name (the first that matches); a structure's own 'purpose' wins.

rooms: one room with a sleeping place

architecture._dressing: (0.4.2, gamefixes: purposeful exterior detail reflecting each place's culture, economy and daily life, without clutter) what each kind of building has about its outside (rpg.world.shadowveil.Dressing): lantern (on the wall by the door), sign (a board on a bracket over the street), woodpile (logs against the gable), hay, shrubs (planting along the front), crates and bench (furniture), timbers (pit-props by a mouth). chance: how likely a building is to have each piece of its list, so a street is not one house repeated.
architecture._farms: (0.4.1) the gardens the growers work (rpg.world.Farming): a grower (rpg.Ids constant), the garden structure, its rows' crops in turn
architecture._views: (0.4.1) four reference cameras for every region and settlement (eye [chunk x, chunk z, height over the ground], look [chunk x, chunk z, height]), each shot in the morning and at night by the gallery (RPG_GALLERY_ONLY=p27) - the reference for every change to an exterior or a terrain.
architecture._later: (0.4.4, gamefixes: each kingdom its own jail with proper cells, its own bankhouse and its own graveyard) A settlement's 'later' buildings are planned after its districts' houses, on the free ground nearest where they are asked for (so the streets already laid stay as they are).
architecture._severia: (0.4.4, gamefixes: Severian architecture must look and resemble Rome and the Byzantine Empire) Severia builds in stucco over Roman brick, its public buildings in Byzantine banded masonry (brick courses between dressed stone) under low hipped roofs of terracotta tile, its floors of fired tile and, in its palace, church, bank and museum, mosaic; its church a domed basilica with a domed bell tower.
